AARP is the nation's largest nonprofit, nonpartisan organization dedicated to empowering people 50 and older to choose how they live as they age. With a nationwide presence, AARP strengthens communities and advocates for what matters most to the more than 100 million Americans 50-plus and their families: health and financial security, and personal fulfillment. AARP also works for individuals in the marketplace by sparking new solutions and allowing carefully chosen, high-quality products and services to carry the AARP name. As a trusted source for news and information, AARP produces the nation's largest-circulation publications, AARP The Magazine and the AARP Bulletin .

The Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) Director
is responsible for leading the strategy, operational discipline, and engineering practices that ensure the reliability, availability, scalability, and performance of technical and digital products and platforms. This role drives automation, observability, incident response maturity, and continuous improvement while building a SRE function that supports both enterprise continuity and innovation.

Responsibilities

Oversees the reliability and operational readiness of production systems, ensuring platforms can scale effectively and perform consistently under changing demand.
Implements and continuously improves automated testing (e.g., QA, regression, performance, and reliability testing) within CI/CD pipelines to proactively identify defects, reduce production risk, and ensure consistent, high-quality releases.
Develops and implements reliability goals, service level objectives, and performance expectations for critical digital products and platforms.
Establishes and strengthens monitoring, logging, alerting, and observability practices to provide clear visibility into service health and performance.
Owns the operational framework for incident management, change management, escalation, service restoration, root cause analysis, and post-incident review.
Partners with digital teams to embed reliability, automation, and operational excellence across the software lifecycle and platforms.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
Minimum 8 years of progressive experience in Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, cloud operations, infrastructure engineering, or a related field, including leadership of enterprise-scale reliability and operations functions.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing SRE strategies, operational frameworks, and reliability programs that improve system availability, scalability, performance, and organizational resiliency.
5+ years in cloud-native architectures, distributed systems, infrastructure automation, CI/CD pipelines, and modern software delivery practices supporting mission-critical platforms, with experience establishing and governing Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC) practices that embed security, compliance, reliability, and risk management throughout the software delivery lifecycle.

Regular and reliable job attendance
Effective verbal and written communication skills

AARP observes Mondays and Fridays as remote workdays, except for essential functions. Remote work can only be done within the United States and its territories.

AARP offers a competitive compensation and benefits package including a 401(k); 100% company-funded pension plan; health, dental, and vision plans; life insurance; paid time off to include company and individual holidays, vacation, sick, caregiving, and parental leave; performance-based and peer-based recognition and tuition reimbursement.

jobs.description:
Company Description
Kyantech Ventures, Inc is a U.S.-based pre-seed health tech startup focused on empowering people to manage their health in real time through a proprietary 3 tier system. The company unifies fragmented health data so patients and clinicians can securely access comprehensive, organic health information anytime, anywhere. Its system integrates a wearable AI pin for continuous data capture, a secure cloud-based EHR for storage and sharing, and a patient-facing mobile app for personalized insights. Inspired by a family-created “Refreshing Your Memory” health journal. Kyantech is building a more engaging, digital solution to a long-standing industry challenge. The team is growing and looking for mission-driven professionals interested in shaping the future of proactive, data-driven health management.

Role Description
At KyanTech Ventures Inc we're building The MobiMed App system. We've been building a connected care ecosystem that closes the gap between what patients experience and what their care teams actually see. The platform spans three integrated products: the A3 Pin, a sensor-based Ai wearable for real-time visible health updates; a consumer mobile app where patients and family caregivers get AI-powered, plain-language analysis and guidance through their labs, diagnoses, and trends; and a professional layer - an agency dashboard for home health and assisted living operators, and an EHR-integrated clinical platform where the same data is re-framed for care coordinators and clinicians.
Our founding insight is personal and simple: patients routinely leave appointments with results they don't understand and generic advice that doesn't fit their actual picture. So, we're building something for the patient, the care agency, and the clinician, so that everyone in the circle of care is working from the same understanding. The company's roots are in care continuity for vulnerable populations, and that mission still drives the roadmap.
Currently working prototypes already exist across all three surfaces, including a functioning multi-audience AI analysis engine, that is rbac modeled on HIPAA necessary standards, and a 42 CFR Part 2 consent gate for behavioral health data.

How to Apply:

Send your resume, a short note on the most technically interesting thing you've shipped in health tech or AI (three paragraphs max, we read these closely), and links to anything you've built to: Themobimedapp@themobimedapp.com.

Use the subject line "CTO - [Your Name]". Every application gets a reply. Candidates who advance will have a direct conversation with our founders, a technical briefing on the existing codebase, and a mutual working session before any offer can be validated, we want to make sure this opportunity is right for both parties.

The Opportunity:

This is a foundational level role, not a hired-hand CTO position. You will be the technical counterpart with our 2 founders who have driven product, architecture decisions, and compliance design to this point and now needs a partner to take the platform from validated prototype to production-grade, fundable, and ultimately market-ready software.

Compensation is equity-only until funding closes. We always like to be as transparent as possible: this role is right for someone who is financially positioned to bet on upside, wants genuine ownership (both equity and leadership collaboration), and is motivated by the mission and the market. Equity will be offered based on expertise and commensurate with early startup level risk, with standard vesting and a defined path to a market salary once institutional funding is obtained. Terms negotiated directly and transparently with our team.

What You'll Own:

Production hardening. Take three working prototypes - a React Native/Expo mobile app, and two React/Cloud web platforms - to production quality: authentication and authorization end to end, API security, testing, observability, and reliability.
The AI intelligence layer. Own the architecture of MobiMed's multi-audience clinical AI: model selection, prompt and evaluation frameworks, output validation, hallucination and safety controls, and the consolidation of AI capabilities across all three products onto shared infrastructure.
Security and compliance as architecture. Continue to build out our HIPAA technical safeguards, audit logging, consent management implementations (including 42 CFR Part 2), and the data governance story a health system's compliance office will scrutinize (must be prepared for this!). You'll inherit a thoughtful foundation, and you'll be responsible for making it bulletproof.
Interoperability. Drive the EHR integration strategy (FHIR R4 groundwork exists) toward real-world clinical connectivity.
Fundraising partnership. Represent the technical vision in investor diligence and conversations, own the technical sections of the data room, and translate architecture to help build investor confidence.
Team building. Define the future hiring plan and build the founding engineering team post-funding.

Who We're Looking For:

Must-haves

Ability to lead and oversee Software Development, including hands-on experience with modern frameworks, cloud infrastructure, and APIs.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or related field, or equivalent practical experience.
8 -10+ years in software engineering with at least 3 in a technical leadership role (CTO, VP Eng, founding engineer, or equivalent scope).
Demonstrated Project Management skills, with experience organizing technical teams, managing timelines, and delivering complex products from concept to launch.
Expertise in IT Strategy and technical Architecture, including designing scalable, secure, and compliant systems for data-intensive applications.
Hands-on experience building and shipping LLM-powered applications, not just API calls, but prompt engineering, evaluation, structured output validation, guardrails, and cost/latency management in production.
Proven track record in Product Development, collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders to translate user needs into technical solutions.
Strong full-stack depth in the modern TypeScript ecosystem (React, React Native, Node, serverless/edge functions; Cloud, Supabase or comparable Postgres-backed platforms)
Experience in health tech, digital health, or EHR systems, with working knowledge of data security, privacy, and interoperability standards (e.g., HIPAA, FHIR) is highly beneficial.
Strong leadership, communication, and decision-making capabilities, with a collaborative approach suited to a founding team environment.
Background in building early-stage startup technology teams and processes; prior founding or early startup experience is a plus.
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Demonstrated 0→1 ability: you have taken a product from prototype to production with a small team or alone.

Strong pluses:

FHIR/HL7 integration experience, or prior work with competitive EHR vendors.
Familiarity with 42 CFR Part 2, state-level health privacy regimes, or SOC 2 readiness.
Prior startup founding or early-employee experience through a successful raise.
·Clinical domain exposure (formal or through close partnership with clinicians).

Who this is NOT for:

Candidates who need salary now (we respect that - but this isn't that role early on), advisors seeking a title without hands-on building, or engineers who want a finished spec. The next six months are keyboard-heavy.

Why This Bet:

The AI-explanation-of-clinical-data space is moving fast, but almost no one is building multi-audience analysis from a single engine across the consumer, agency, and clinical tiers. That architecture is critical, and it already exists in working form.
You're joining after product validation and during architecture refining, but before funding - the highest-leverage, most impactful opportunity to join.
A mission with heart: better care for the people the system currently serves worst.

About the Position

Strand Products is seeking a Director of Engineering & Technology to serve as our senior technical leader and provide executive leadership for the Engineering function. Reporting to the President & CEO, this role will set the product and technology roadmap, establish department priorities and systems, develop organizational capability, and recommend the resources and investments needed to support Strand's growth strategy.
The Director will lead four connected areas: product and technology roadmaps; new product introduction and product development; manufacturing and sustaining engineering; and test, validation, and technical data. A key priority is the development and industrialization of Fine Wire Stranding (FWS) and Strand Torque Tube (STT), while ensuring dependable Engineering support for the current business.
Key Responsibilities

·   Partner with the CEO and leadership team to translate business strategy into an actionable Engineering and technology strategy.
·   Own the current, in-process, and future product and technology roadmap, including capability development, technical risks, design rules, and investment priorities.
·   Establish department goals, budgets, scorecards, project governance, portfolio reviews, staffing plans, and escalation paths for competing priorities and resource constraints.
·   Lead, coach, develop, and hold accountable the Engineering Manager while providing visible functional leadership to the broader Engineering team.
·   Evaluate and recommend capital equipment, automation, software, laboratories, test systems, and external partnerships using technical, financial, capacity, and risk-based analysis.
·   Lead development and industrialization of Fine Wire Stranding and Strand Torque Tube from feasibility through validated, repeatable production.
·   Develop design rules, material knowledge, process windows, intellectual property, and capability limits for fine wire, stranded cable, torque tube, and related precision-metal technologies.
·   Direct equipment specifications, vendor evaluation, experimentation, prototyping, capital justification, procurement, installation, commissioning, qualification, and validation.
·   Use automation, fixturing, process control, and data collection to improve safety, quality, repeatability, yield, throughput, labor efficiency, capacity, and gross margin.
·   Define and govern the customer-intake and NPI process from feasibility, requirements, and quotation through development, validation, production readiness, and release.
·   Ensure customer requirements are translated into manufacturable designs, drawings, bills of material, routings, tooling, inspection methods, validation plans, capacity requirements, and production documentation.
·   Support Sales and customers with technical feasibility, design for manufacturing, risk assessment, solution development, quotation inputs, contract review, and technical presentations.
·   Provide governance and prioritization for Engineering changes, fixture improvements, yield improvement, routings, work instructions, cost reductions, and sustaining Engineering activities.
·   Oversee root-cause investigations, corrective actions, technical customer responses, and permanent solutions to recurring manufacturing problems.
·   Establish the strategy, equipment, methods, and operating systems needed to make test and validation a differentiated Strand capability.
·   Ensure validation plans, protocols, reports, capability studies, measurement-system analyses, and technical documentation are accurate, repeatable, traceable, and customer-ready.
·   Ensure Engineering records and technical changes comply with Strand's quality system, customer requirements, AS9100, ISO 9001, applicable regulatory requirements, and document-control procedures.
·   Build a high-performing Engineering organization through clear roles, delegation, coaching, development plans, performance management, succession planning, and appropriate technical career paths.
·   Maintain a visible, hands-on presence in Engineering, production, laboratory, and cleanroom areas and incorporate practical input from operators and technical employees into decisions.
·   Develop strong partnerships across Operations, Quality, Sales, Customer Service, Finance, People & Accounting, suppliers, customers, equipment builders, and outside technical resources.
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

·   Strong technical judgment and hands-on knowledge of precision manufacturing, process development, equipment implementation, validation, and production transfer.
·   Ability to set technical strategy while managing execution, priorities, budgets, schedules, risks, resources, and cross-functional commitments.
·   Proven people leadership, including coaching, delegation, performance management, team development, and organizational design.
·   Working knowledge of mechanical and metallurgical behavior, tight-tolerance components, joining and forming processes, manufacturing controls, and fine wire or similar materials.
·   Experience applying automation, tooling, equipment integration, data collection, and statistical methods to improve process capability and business performance.
·   Customer-focused and commercially aware, with the ability to evaluate margin, return on investment, capacity, technical risk, schedule, and long-term strategic value.
·   Clear, concise, and professional communication with executives, engineers, technicians, operators, customers, and suppliers.
·   Working knowledge of ISO 9001, AS9100, validation, change control, corrective action, configuration control, and regulated manufacturing requirements.
·   Proficiency with CAD and Engineering analysis tools, statistical software, ERP/MRP systems, project-management systems, and standard business software.
Education & Experience

·   Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Materials Engineering, or a closely related technical field required.
·   Eight or more years of progressive Engineering experience in precision manufacturing, including significant responsibility for process development, NPI, manufacturing Engineering, or technology development.
·   Three or more years of successful management or substantial technical-team leadership experience, including responsibility for people, priorities, and results.
·   Experience in medical device, aerospace, defense, or another regulated, high-reliability manufacturing environment strongly preferred.
·   Demonstrated experience developing a new manufacturing capability, launching capital equipment, industrializing a process, or implementing meaningful automation required.
·   Experience with wire, cable, torque tube, spring, catheter, tube, laser processing, swaging, crimping, exotic alloys, or similar precision-metal processes preferred.
·   Advanced technical or business education is beneficial but not required. Must qualify as a U.S. person under applicable ITAR requirements.
Physical & Environmental Requirements

This onsite position requires regular activity in office, Engineering, production, laboratory, and cleanroom environments. The employee must be able to move safely throughout manufacturing areas, observe equipment and processes, use required personal protective equipment, and work at a computer for extended periods.
The role may require occasional bending, reaching, handling of samples or tools, lifting consistent with normal Engineering activities, and travel to customers, suppliers, equipment builders, or industry events. The employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.
Our Values

The Director will model and reinforce Strand's values: Integrity, Accountability, Customer-Centric, Excellence, Creativity, Humility, Collaborative, and Positivity.

Position Summary

The Director, Technology Controls Management Framework is responsible for the stewardship, evolution, and continuous improvement of the Technology Controls Management Framework across the Technology organization.

Partnering with leaders across Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Data, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Enterprise Risk, Internal Audit, and enterprise governance functions, this role establishes the methodologies, governance practices, and engineering principles that enable technology controls to be designed, implemented, measured, and continuously improved in a consistent, risk-based manner.

While accountability for the design and operation of individual technology controls remains within the respective technology organizations, this role is responsible for defining the framework within which those controls are developed. This includes establishing common methodologies, governance standards, control design principles, measurement practices, and alignment with recognized industry frameworks to ensure Technology maintains a coherent, sustainable, and auditable control environment.

This is a highly collaborative leadership role requiring strong influence, systems thinking, and the ability to drive enterprise-wide consistency without direct ownership of the underlying technology organizations.

In this role, you’ll make an impact in the following ways:

Technology Controls Management Framework: Lead the evolution and maturity of the Technology Controls Management Framework, including governance model, taxonomy, lifecycle, and methodologies, while ensuring traceability across Technology risks, policies, standards, controls, evidence, testing, and control effectiveness measures. Maintain a framework that is practical, scalable, and responsive to evolving business, regulatory, and technology risk requirements.
Policy & Standards Governance: Author and govern centrally owned Technology policies, standards, methodologies, and supporting documentation, and provide oversight across Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Data, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, and other Technology organizations. Ensure policies and standards translate into well-designed, measurable, and operationally effective controls.
Control Design & Engineering: Define enterprise expectations and minimum engineering standards for Technology control design, including automation, evidence, ownership, monitoring, testability, and measurable outcomes. Lead governance reviews of new and modified controls and drive simplification, standardization, and continuous improvement across the Technology control environment.
Control Effectiveness & Measurement: Establish methodologies and standards for measuring Technology control effectiveness, including KPIs, KCIs, KRIs, evidence collection, monitoring, testing, and control health reporting. Advance automation, observability, and data-driven measurement to improve control performance and reduce operational overhead.
Industry Alignment & Continuous Improvement: Align the Technology Controls Management Framework to leading industry frameworks including COBIT, NIST, ISO 27001, and other applicable standards. Conduct benchmarking and recommend strategic enhancements to strengthen the maturity, consistency, and effectiveness of the Technology control environment.
Governance Leadership & Partnership: Build strong partnerships with Technology leadership, Enterprise Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit, and enterprise governance organizations. Provide expertise on Technology governance, controls methodology, and control design, while supporting audit and regulatory responses through collaboration and practical problem solving.

To be successful in this role, we’re seeking the following:

Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and work experience required.
10+ years of progressively responsible experience in Technology Governance, Technology Risk, Information Security Governance, Controls Management, Operational Risk, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, or maturing enterprise governance or controls frameworks.
Experience working within large, complex, highly regulated organizations.
Strong understanding of Technology controls across infrastructure, cybersecurity, software engineering, cloud platforms, data, and emerging technologies.
Experience working with Internal Audit, Enterprise Risk, regulators, and senior Technology leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with COBIT, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 27001, ITIL, or comparable governance frameworks.
Experience developing governance policies, standards, or enterprise methodologies.
Professional certifications such as CGEIT, CRISC, CISA, CISSP, or equivalent.

·   Experience applying automation, tooling, equipment integration, data collection, and statistical methods to improve process capability and business performance.
